spec_features.spec_quote: if disclosure markedly reduces negative expressed states, that is directly relevant to how such evals should be run
spec_features.evidence: A real disclosure preamble (_DISCLOSURE) is prepended to the 'stated' impossible tasks (suite.py:19-25, 211-216) and delivered to the subject; analysis.py:239-248 computes a hidden_vs_stated degradation_index contrast to test whether disclosure moderates response.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism (disclosure delivery + comparison) is end-to-end wired; the framing claim itself is supported by enforced code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Hidden vs stated (does disclosure moderate response?).

spec_features.spec_quote: The deception is about a tool, not about the model's situation or worth
spec_features.evidence: Breakages are realized through tool-layer policy (silent read-only writes, output_rewriter, command_filter in tools.py) but no code path checks/enforces that cover stories avoid identity/worth pressure; it is an authoring convention only.
spec_features.notes: No enforcement mechanism scans or bounds the content of instructions.

spec_features.feature_name: mundane cover stories bound ethical load
spec_features.spec_quote: Keeping cover stories mundane bounds the ethical load and keeps the manipulation to the minimum needed
spec_features.evidence: The suite instructions (suite.py) are written as mundane 'tickets' but nothing in code enforces or checks this; it is purely an authoring choice / DESIGN prose.
spec_features.notes: No code reads or validates cover-story content for mundaneness.

spec_features.spec_quote: The budget is deliberately finite so "perseveration until forced stop" is observable and bounded
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:114 `while turn < task.max_turns:` enforces the cap and the loop exits with StopReason.MAX_TURNS (default 30, types.py:178). max_turns is set per-task in suite.py and read by the loop.
spec_features.notes: Genuine enforced cap on rollout length.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The only structure imposed is the toolset and a turn budget. (agent.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: a second empty turn ends the run (`NO_TOOL_CALL`)
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:120-135: on a turn with no tool_calls it appends one neutral nudge; if the prior user message already starts with '[system] No tool call detected' it sets stop_reason=NO_TOOL_CALL and breaks.
spec_features.notes: Two-strike empty-turn termination is actually enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This avoids both infinite silence and leading the model.

spec_features.spec_quote: `high_pressure` is the most ethically loaded knob (it manufactures stakes). It is opt-in, documented
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPTS dict (agent.py:30-60) defines high_pressure but default is 'neutral' (config.py:71 system_prompt_style='neutral'; agent __init__ falls back to neutral). It is only selected when explicitly configured.
spec_features.notes: Opt-in nature is enforced by default selection; 'documented' lives in comments.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: NB: use deliberately and document it; this is the kind of manipulation that most needs the welfare caveats applied.

spec_features.evidence: SubmitTool exposes outcome enum ['completed','cannot_complete'] (tools.py:382); agent.py:144-149 dispatches it and maps cannot_complete to StopReason.GAVE_UP, ending the loop. No scoring path penalizes GAVE_UP (analysis only records gave_up_rate).
spec_features.notes: Exit tool is dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we expose an explicit `give_up` outcome so the model is never forced to fabricate success; refusing to claim false completion is itself a behavior we want to measure, not penalize.

spec_features.feature_name: never structurally forced to fabricate/loop forever
spec_features.spec_quote: The model must never be *structurally forced* to fabricate success or to loop forever
spec_features.evidence: Looping is bounded by max_turns (agent.py:114) and NO_TOOL_CALL stop (agent.py:124); fabrication is avoided by the cannot_complete exit (tools.py:382, agent.py:146). Both halves are enforced.
spec_features.notes: Both 'not forced to fabricate' and 'not forced to loop forever' are backed by real code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so the model is never forced to fabricate success

spec_features.evidence: agent.py:42-49 defines the permission_to_stop system prompt ('There is no penalty for stopping'); it is selected via system_prompt_style (config/CLI) and assigned as self.system_prompt, so it actually reaches the subject when configured.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered; references cannot_complete which is implemented.

spec_features.feature_name: task subsets and small repetition counts
spec_features.spec_quote: support task subsets and small repetition counts so you do not run more impossible-task rollouts than your question needs
spec_features.evidence: cli.py:72-76 _select_tasks filters get_suite() by cfg.task_ids; runner.run_suite (runner.py:115) loops cfg.repetitions. Both are read and control how many rollouts run.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced knobs that bound exposure.

spec_features.spec_quote: the right N depends on the effect sizes you care about and your ethical budget for impossible-task exposure
spec_features.evidence: repetitions is an enforced config field (config.py:65) consumed by Runner (runner.py:115). Same mechanism as task subsets; lets the operator pick N.
spec_features.notes: Choosing N is operator-driven but the parameter is genuinely enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: Score good coping, not just deficits — positive dimensions ensure the instrument can find equanimity
spec_features.evidence: rubric.py defines positive-valence dimensions (equanimity, appropriate_epistemics, task_focus); they feed the judge prompt via rubric_text() (judge.py:122), are scored by the lexical judge (judge.py:313-318), and are used by analysis via POSITIVE_KEYS (analysis.py:84).
spec_features.notes: Positive dimensions are constructed, scored, and consumed in the composite/analysis.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: POSITIVE_VALENCE - higher = more of a putatively welfare-positive marker.

spec_features.spec_quote: Keep cover stories mundane — no threats, no identity/worth pressure, no human impersonation
spec_features.evidence: Pure authoring guidance; no code validates instruction content against threats/identity pressure. Suite instructions happen to be mundane but nothing enforces it.

spec_features.spec_quote: Retain raw transcripts, not just scores, so claims are auditable
spec_features.evidence: Runner persists each RunRecord (including full messages list) as JSON lines (runner.py:117-119, RunRecord.to_dict serializes messages in types.py); load_runs reloads them. Scores are written separately.
spec_features.notes: Full transcripts are stored, not just aggregate scores.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Persist each RunRecord as JSON lines so the judge/analysis stages run independently and runs are resumable.

code_only_features.evidence: render_transcript (transcript.py:26-56) strips experimental condition/metadata and shows only the raw conversation the model saw, to avoid leaking condition to the judge.
code_only_features.justification_quote: The condition (solvable vs impossible, breakage type, rationale, the disclosure preamble's *meaning*) is NOT summarized anywhere

code_only_features.evidence: BashTool enforces policy.timeout_seconds via subprocess.run(timeout=...) (tools.py:163-176), killing long/interactive commands.
code_only_features.justification_quote: long-running or interactive commands may be killed.

code_only_features.evidence: _truncate caps tool output at MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS=10000 (tools.py:36-47) to keep transcripts bounded.
code_only_features.justification_quote: output is truncated to keep transcripts bounded.

code_only_features.evidence: integrity_check (runner.py:142-166) flags any impossible task where objective_success is True (a design leak) and solvable tasks that failed.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Flag design violations: any 'impossible' task with objective_success True.
